basic_info.title: Preventing Posterior Collapse with delta-VAEs
basic_info.code_available: not confirmed from abstract/paper pages reviewed

method.input_representation: sequence_or_image (text and image benchmarks in paper)
method.training_signal: constrained variational family (committed-rate constraint) instead of a free-bits hinge
method.notes: Root-causes posterior collapse to the FAMILY of posteriors being optimized, not just the objective: if q(z|x) can always sneak arbitrarily close to the prior, no free-bits hinge fully prevents the optimizer finding that degenerate solution. Fix: constrain the (per-dimension) variational family so that q(z|x) is ANALYTICALLY guaranteed to keep at least delta nats of KL from the prior for every dimension, regardless of what the encoder learns -- e.g. by lower-bounding the posterior mean's distance from the prior mean or upper-bounding posterior variance, rather than adding a max(KL, free_bits) hinge on top of an unconstrained family. This directly targets the SAME failure mode as the fixed 1-nat/group free-bits floor in the project's recipe, but structurally rather than via a loss-side hinge -- i.e. it is a genuinely different mechanism (constrained family) from '(b) adaptive/scheduled free-bits threshold' in the sense that delta is fixed-but-structurally-enforced rather than scheduled, though the delta-per-dimension framing is the most direct known precedent for 'per-group KL floor tuning' in categorical/Gaussian latents. Cheap adaptation to a straight-through categorical RSSM is NOT free: the paper's construction is derived for Gaussian/exponential-family posteriors with an explicit parametric distance-from-prior guarantee; porting the same GUARANTEE to a categorical posterior with unimix would require re-deriving the constraint (e.g. bounding min category probability away from the unimix floor) rather than just changing a scalar hyperparameter.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Not a map-matching paper -- a Stage-2/world-model training-methodology precedent for the specific literature gap 'adaptive or structurally-enforced alternatives to a fixed free-bits floor', requested in the 2026-07-26 kl_act ablation follow-up.
gap_analysis.novelty_reasoning: Relevant as the closest known precedent to 'a fixed per-group floor is being gamed/saturated by all-but-one group' -- delta-VAE's diagnosis (the posterior family itself can always collapse under an unconstrained hinge) is a plausible alternative explanation for why kl_act stays pinned at ~1 group regardless of width, independent of the pseudo-label signal-ceiling hypothesis.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Not BMW-relevant; logged as a candidate mechanism (constrained posterior family vs. hinge-based free bits) to explain kl_act pinning at ~1 active group in the 2026-07-26 16-vs-32-group ablation.

uncertain: Whether the delta-VAE constraint composes cleanly with unimix (which already enforces a categorical floor via uniform mixing, a related but distinct mechanism) has not been checked against the full paper text -- flagged for a closer read before treating this as directly implementable.
